newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKEES DH FIELDER HAS THUMB SURGERY, OUT 6-TO-8 WEEKS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKEES DH FIELDER HAS THUMB SURGERY, OUT 6-TO-8 WEEKS.

text.p: New York Yankees designated hitter Cecil Fielder had surgery on his ailing right thumb Thursday and is expected to be out six to eight weeks.
The 33-year-old Fielder suffered a fracture and ligament damage in his thumb while making an awkward headfirst slide into home plate in Tuesday's 12-6 victory over Cleveland.
Fielder, a big-time slugger who has suffered through a power shortage this season, was placed on the disabled list Wednesday for the first time in his career.

"I am very disappointed, this season has been frustrating from Day One," Fielder said. "It kind of bums you out but I have to take care of my hand and do what the doctors order. They (the doctors) told me if I didn't get the injury fixed it would heal, but my (thumb) wouldn't be attached properly."
The portly slugger, who has become a favourite target of disgruntled fans at Yankee Stadium, is batting .254 with only 10 homers and 51 RBI in 87 games.

Fielder is making $9.2 million in the final year of his contract and angered fans in the offseason when he threatened to exercise a clause that allowed him to become a free agent if he was not traded. He later backed off that demand.

To replace Fielder on the roster, the Yankees purchased the contract of 29-year-old first baseman Ivan Cruz from Triple-A Columbus. Cruz was batting .312 with 22 homers and 87 RBI in 92 games with the Clippers.
